source_text: Nec peccare eos omnino, qui peccare dicuntur: siquidem a quocumque creati sunt, secundum id quod creati sunt, necesse habent vivere, nec suae repugnare naturae
pass_a_gloss: Nor peccare them entirely, who peccare they-say: siquidem from quocumque creati are, according-to it that/which creati are, necessary have to-live, nor his-own to-fight-against of-nature.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: Those who are said to sin are not sinning at all, if, whoever created them, they must live according to the way they were created and cannot resist their own nature.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
